data.narrative:
Machina Labs is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $80M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable in the robotics sector, including same-stage peers Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B) and Dexterity ($1.6B), as well as adjacent-stage companies Hadrian ($1.6B) and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B).

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach, anchoring on total capital raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.9x multiplier typical for Series B advancement, yielding $152M. The peer-median method references the four-company comparable set, which shows a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.0B to $1.8B, reflecting the wide spread in recent robotics financings at similar stages. The peer-median method is particularly applicable given the availability of recent, same-sector transactions.

Triangulation of these two methods produces a valuation range of $129M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $888M. The stage-progression method implies a substantially lower value than peer comparables, reflecting the stage-based methodology's sensitivity to capital raised rather than market multiples. The gap between methods highlights the key uncertainty: whether Machina Labs' operational progress and market position align with the valuation benchmarks set by higher-funded peers, or whether it warrants a discount to the peer median pending further technical or commercial validation.
